newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coffee waits for London to gather steam.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coffee waits for London to gather steam.

text.p: A price mismatch between robusta coffee buyers and sellers in Indonesia brought the market to a standstill on Monday as players anxiously waited for direction from the London futures market, traders said.
"There have been no trades so far today," one trader said. "The gap between buyers' bids and sellers' offers is very wide and there is nothing happening in the market."
The traders said grade four robusta was quoted at 4,100-4,200 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 4,250-4,300 rupiah a week ago.
Exporters were seeking to buy at $1,700-$1,750 a tonne fob Lampung while sellers were asking for $1,825-$1,850, compared with a traded price of $1,950 last week.
"Where the price will head will depend how the London market does later today," one trader said.
The traders said London's benchmark July robusta coffee contract was expected to rise when the market opens later on Monday in a rebound after last Friday's sharp decline.
"London's July is due to increase by about $60," one trader said. But others said they expected a more modest increase of between $30 to $40.
The traders said the Indonesian market was quiet, as sellers held back transactions in the face of what they considered were low bids from buyers.

"Sellers who have the cash flow are holding back sales because bids by buyers were considered low," one trader said. "Buyers, on the other hand, are not buying because they feel the sellers' offer prices are too high."
"At this point, we have a market that seems to be at a standstill because of this difference," he added.
Another trader said sellers found the $1,825-$1,850 a tonne price too high compared with the closing price of London's July contract last Friday.

The July contract closed $80 down on the day at $1,825 a tonne after hitting a low of $1,815 last Friday. Later in the day, New York arabica coffee rose 6.75 cents a lb higher to close at 237.25 cents in a technical correction.
One trader said supply in Indonesia was beginning to tighten due to a production shortfall.

"Sellers are optimistic that tightening supply will lift robusta prices over the next few months," he said. "Why should a farmer sell at low prices now when he feels he can get a better price a little further down the road."
The traders said players were also watching closely weather developments in Brazil, the top exporter, where farmers in some regions went on alert on Sunday for possible frost.

In Tres Pontas, southern Minas Gerais state, producers were bringing out cloud-forming machines as temperatures fell but meteorologists forecast that any freezes were most likely to occur in lower-lying areas where coffee was not generally grown.
"Any incidence of frosts in Brazil will change the entire equation," one Indonesian trader said. "Players are closely watching the situation in Brazil."
